newsitem.title: USA: Chevron says makes "significant" Angola find.
newsitem.headline: Chevron says makes "significant" Angola find.

text.p: Chevron Corp on Tuesday announced a "significant" discovery of crude oil in waters more than 1,300 feet deep off Angola, its first deep-water find in that country.
The new discovery, designated well 14-2X, is the second of five wells planned in Block 14, an deepwater oil patch offshore the Cabinda Province.
"Early tests encountered a significant oil-bearing interval which suggests this could be a giant field," said Dick Matzke, a director of Chevron Corp. and president of Chevron Overseas Petroleum Inc.
Initial tests showed a combined flow rate of about 7,500 barrels of oil per day. The 14-2X well was preceded by the 14-1X well, which also produced hydrocarbons.
Matzke said the site needs more appraisal to confirm oil reserves and determine plans for development.
Chevron is the operator and holds 31 percent interest in Block 14.

Sociedade Nacional de Combusteiveis de Angola (SONANGOL), the Angolan national oil company, Agip Angola, and Total Angola each hold a 20 percent interest. The remaining 9 percent interest is held by Petrogal Angola.
